faq.title: Questions
faq.a1: Open the sign-up page and enter an email, a username, and a password. The first account on an empty database is the admin. The server can close registration after that. The steps from sign-up through the first chapter are in the {guide}.
faq.q2: Do I need my own key?
faq.a2: Yes. In Settings, fill in the provider, the base URL, and the key, then pick models for tasks such as generating and checking. Then you can start writing.
faq.q3: Can I keep the key off the server?
faq.a3: Yes. Choose “Keep only in this browser”. If you clear site data or switch browsers, you enter it again.
faq.q4: Can other people see my book?
faq.a4: No. Each account can open only its own books.
faq.q5: Can I write on a phone?
faq.a5: Yes. Open it in the phone’s browser. While you write, the prose fills the screen, and the outline, character cards, and foreshadows can be edited full screen.

prepare.title: Before you start
prepare.key: You need an API key from a model provider. OpenRouter, Volcengine Ark, and other OpenAI-compatible APIs are supported. The provider bills you for model use.
prepare.privacy: Each book belongs only to your account. Other people cannot open your outline, prose, or memory.

register.title: 1. Sign up and log in
register.step1: On the home page, click “Sign up”.
register.step2: Enter an email, a username, and a password. Usernames are 2 to 32 characters and may include Chinese, letters, digits, underscores, and hyphens. Passwords must be at least 8 characters.
register.step3: Click “Sign up”. You land on the bookshelf.
register.step4: Next time, click “Log in” on the home page. Email or username both work, with the same password.

model.title: 2. Set up a model
model.lead: If there is no key, or a task has no model, generating and checking stop and tell you nothing is configured yet. Finish this step before you write chapter 1.
model.where: On a computer, click the gear at the top right of the bookshelf to open Settings. On a phone, open a book first, then tap More at the bottom and Settings. The first item on the left is “Model and keys”.
model.provider: Click “＋ Provider”. For Volcengine Ark, click “＋ Volcengine Ark”. The API base URL is filled in as {ark}. For any other provider, enter the base URL yourself. It usually ends with {v1}. You can add up to 5 providers.
model.store: Choose where the key is stored.
model.server: “Save on the server (encrypted)”: it still works after you log in on another computer or phone. Exported books do not include the key.
model.browser: “Keep only in this browser”: the server does not store this key. If you clear site data, switch browsers, or switch devices, you fill it in again. Calls are still relayed through the server to the provider, but the key is not saved.
model.test: Click “Test”. When the base URL and key work, the status becomes Connected. If you also filled in a model id, the test tries that id once more.
model.tasksIntro: On the right, under “Model for each task”, set all five:
model.taskGenerate: Generate prose: for writing chapters. Prefer strong prose at a lower cost.
model.taskCheck: Consistency check: compares the draft with memory and looks for contradictions. Prefer strong reasoning.
model.taskExtract: Extract memory changes: pulls character and setting changes out of the prose. Prefer strong reasoning.
model.taskSummary: Chapter summary: a recap for later chapters. A cheaper model is enough.
model.taskChat: Chat with AI: for the outline, the chapter outline, and characters. If you do not pick one, the “Generate prose” model is used.
model.catalog: Providers such as OpenRouter load a model list when the page opens, so you can search and pick one. Volcengine Ark does not load a list. Copy the Model ID from the {docs} and paste it onto the matching task.

book.title: 3. Create a book
book.chat: To talk the premise through first, click “Talk through a new book idea”. The model asks about genre, the hook, the protagonist, the world, the special advantage, the core conflict, and the opening. It only suggests. Nothing is saved until you apply it. When the plan looks right, create the book from it. That chat does not belong to any book. It stays on the bookshelf under the title Idea.
book.self: To create it yourself, click “＋ New book”.
book.fields: Enter a title. The default target is 2,500 words per chapter, from 300 to 20,000. The foreshadow reminder defaults to 3 chapters, meaning the warning starts 3 chapters before the planned payoff. Any value from 0 to 50 is allowed.
book.create: Click “Create”. The app places empty templates for the world, the overall outline, and “Volume 1”, and starts version history.
book.shelf: Each book on the bookshelf shows how many chapters are confirmed and the word count. A must-fix issue, or an overdue foreshadow, is marked on the card. “Continue chapter N” returns to the chapter that is not confirmed yet.

outline.title: 4. Write the outline and the chapter outline
outline.lead: After you open a book, the top bar is Write, Memory, Foreshadows, Outline, and Stats. Go to Outline first, write what happens in this chapter, then generate the prose.
outline.tree: Down the left side: World, Overall outline, Volumes, then each chapter. “＋ Chapter outline” adds a chapter. “＋ Volume” adds a volume.
outline.layers: The world is included every time a chapter is generated. The overall outline is the direction of the whole book. A volume has a name, a goal for that volume, and a volume outline. Markdown is supported.
outline.fillIntro: Click a chapter and fill in the chapter outline:
outline.goal: Goal for this chapter: what this chapter has to accomplish
outline.payoff: Payoff: the moment the reader enjoys most
outline.hook: End hook: the question that makes someone want the next chapter
outline.cast: Characters on stage: pick from existing character cards, or type a new name. If there is no card, the page offers to create one, or to switch to an existing character with a similar name.
outline.length: Length for this chapter: leave it blank to use the book default.
outline.linked: Linked foreshadows: these are included when you generate. Foreshadows nearing their payoff are included automatically too.
outline.ai: While a section is still the empty template, you can click “Fill with AI” or “Chat with AI”. The model first explains in plain language. A change is written only after you click “Apply”, and it leaves a version you can undo. Ignore means nothing changes.
outline.generate: When the chapter outline is ready, click “Generate this chapter” to open the writing page. If the chapter already has prose, the button says “Writing page”.
outline.rewrite: Editing the outline or the chapter outline does not rewrite chapters that are already drafted. To change the prose, open the writing page and click “Regenerate”.

write.title: 5. Write the prose
write.lead: The writing page has a step bar: Chapter outline, Generate, Revise, Check, Confirm changes. The current step is highlighted. Finished steps get a check.
write.list: The chapter list is on the left. If there are no chapters yet, click “+ New chapter” at the top left, or write a chapter outline on the Outline page first.
write.context: Before you generate, check the two tabs on the right. “Chapter outline” is this chapter’s goal, conflict, payoff, and hook. “Injected context” is the characters, settings, foreshadows, and earlier summaries sent to the model this time. Fix anything that looks wrong, then generate.
write.generate: Click “Generate prose”. Reasoning is shown above the prose and is not mixed into it. Once words start coming out, the reasoning area collapses to one line: “Done thinking. Writing the prose.”
write.continue: If the draft is still short of this chapter’s target, click “Continue generating”. It writes on from the last sentence and does not repeat what is already there.
write.regenerate: “Regenerate” rewrites the whole chapter. Prose you already edited is replaced.
write.stop: “Stop generating” stops at the current text. What was already written is saved as a draft.
write.background: If you close the page, or the connection drops, this generation keeps going in the background. Open the chapter again and the draft that was written is there.
write.manual: To write it yourself: on an empty chapter click “Write it myself”. If prose already exists, click “Edit prose” or double-click the prose. One paragraph per line, with a line break between paragraphs. Typing saves automatically, and the save state is shown beside it.

check.title: 6. Run a consistency check
check.lead: When the prose is ready, click “Consistency check” at the top right. It looks for real contradictions against memory. It does not judge the writing. It checks whether speech and actions match the character, whether the draft conflicts with existing settings (timeline, power level, place, rules), whether someone who is dead or already offstage appears again, and whether a catchphrase repeats too often. If a dead or offstage person appears in the prose, the rule reports it even when the model does not. A flashback can be marked as a false positive.
check.levels: Issues come in three levels: Must fix, Should fix, and Hint. A marker sits after the matching paragraph. “Show in the text” on the right scrolls to that paragraph.
check.card: For a character issue you can “View character card”.
check.falsePositive: If the judgment is wrong, “Mark as a false positive”. Reasons: written this way on purpose, the check misread the text, the memory is out of date, or other. You can add one line of detail. After you check “Don’t flag this kind of issue again in this chapter”, that chapter will not report the same case.
check.changed: If the prose changes after the check, check again before you confirm. The right side says “The text changed after the check”.
check.blocked: You cannot confirm the chapter while a “Must fix” issue is still open. Change the prose, or mark it as a false positive, then check again.

confirm.title: 7. Confirm memory changes
confirm.lead: After the check passes, “Confirm memory changes” at the bottom right can be clicked. A line under the button explains a gray button: there is no prose yet, it has not been checked, the prose changed and needs another check, or a must-fix issue is still open.
confirm.extract: On the confirm page, the app extracts changes from this chapter’s prose. Wait while it extracts. If it fails, retry, or “Skip the model and only record who appears”.
confirm.reviewIntro: On the left, “Needs your decision” lists the important changes. Handle them one by one:
confirm.alive: Whether a character is alive, present, and their power level
confirm.hooks: New foreshadows and foreshadows paid off
confirm.reviewTail: Each item can be accepted, edited, rejected, or left for later. Shortcuts: A accept, E edit, R reject. For a new foreshadow you can edit the text and enter the chapter planned for the payoff.
confirm.auto: On the right, “Accepted automatically” is ordinary state, such as location, injuries, and items held. Those are accepted by default. Undo one if it looks wrong.
confirm.commit: When you are done, click confirm. Accepted changes are written into memory. This chapter gets a version you can roll back. Its status becomes confirmed, and the prose is read-only.
confirm.summary: After confirmation, a summary of this chapter is generated for later chapters. If the summary fails, the confirmation is not undone. If the done page says the summary was not generated, click “Regenerate summary”. You can generate it again from the summary tab in Memory too.
confirm.next: On the done page, “Write chapter N” goes to the next chapter, or “View the text” comes back to read. Only confirmed chapters can be exported as TXT. Range and whether to merge them are chosen on the done page.
confirm.undo: If later chapters are not confirmed yet, you can “Undo this chapter’s confirmation”. If a later chapter is already confirmed, you cannot undo this chapter alone. To edit confirmed prose, undo the confirmation first.

memory.title: 8. Memory
memory.tabs: Click “Memory” at the top. Three tabs on the left: Characters, Settings, and Summaries. You can search.
memory.cards: A character card stores role, appearance, personality, catchphrase, arc, and relationships. Current state includes alive, present, power level, location, injuries, items held, and last seen. Alive, present, and power level are locked: those changes must be accepted by hand when you confirm the chapter.
memory.settings: Setting cards are categorized as place, faction, item, rule, timeline, power system, or other. With “Always include” checked, every later chapter generation carries this card. Rules are a good fit for that.
memory.create: Click “＋ New character card” or “＋ New setting card”. An empty card can use “Fill with AI” or “Chat with AI”. It is written only after you apply.
memory.summaries: Summaries appear after a chapter is confirmed. When a new chapter is generated, summaries of the latest few chapters are included.
memory.edits: Editing a card directly here does not leave a version. State changes that happen in the prose should go through the confirmation in step 7. A card the AI changed can be undone in version history.

foreshadow.title: 9. Foreshadows
foreshadow.add: New foreshadows you accept while confirming a chapter land in this list. You can also click “＋ Add a foreshadow”.
foreshadow.fields: Each row has an id, the text, related characters, the chapter where it was planted, and the chapter planned for the payoff. Status is open, paid off, or abandoned.
foreshadow.stats: The top of the page counts overdue and still open, due soon inside the reminder window, open, paid off, and the payoff rate. Filter by status or by character.
foreshadow.actions: Under “Actions” you can edit, mark paid off, abandon, set back to open, or delete.
foreshadow.timing: If the chapter you are writing has passed the planned payoff chapter, it is overdue. If it has not arrived yet but is inside the early-reminder window, it is due soon. The bookshelf also shows how many are overdue.

after.title: 10. Stats, export, versions, and account
after.search: After you open a book, Search sits to the left of the gear on a computer. On a phone it is under More at the bottom. You can search prose, summaries, the outline and chapter outlines, character cards, setting cards, and foreshadows. A result opens the matching chapter, card, or foreshadow. A prose result scrolls to that paragraph.
after.read: “Read” is in the top navigation. On a phone it is under More. Only confirmed chapters are laid out here, volume by volume. To change a chapter, click “Writing page” beside it.
after.stats: “Stats” at the top totals tokens per chapter, the hand-edit share (how much of the generated draft you changed), and confirmed words. A dark bar means the same chapter was regenerated more than twice. The provider bills you for model use.
after.tests: “Buried-error test set” on the same page shows how many mistakes you hid on purpose the consistency check misses. You can ignore it for ordinary writing. It is more useful after you change how checking is used.
after.exportZip: Each book on the bookshelf has “Export the whole book”. It is also under “Book settings” on the in-book settings page. The export is a zip: confirmed chapters are Markdown, and character cards, settings, foreshadows, summaries, and the outline are YAML.
after.exportTxt: The done page after a chapter is confirmed can “Export TXT”. Only confirmed chapters are included, and you can choose the range.
after.versions: Open it from “Version history” on the left of Settings, or from “Version history” in Memory. Each chapter confirmation, and each outline or card the AI changed, leaves an entry. Open one to see what changed. Undoing a whole entry has to start from the newest version that has not been undone, then move backward. Character cards and setting cards can also “Restore only this card”. After a chapter is confirmed, you cannot undo that chapter alone if a later chapter is already confirmed.
after.book: After you open a book, the gear at the top right includes “Book settings”. You can change the title, the target length per chapter, and how early foreshadows are reminded. Deleting the book asks you to type the title. Prose, memory, foreshadows, and versions are deleted together.
after.profile: Click the avatar at the top right and choose “Profile”. Pick an avatar from the presets. The default is the first letter of the username. The username can be changed only once. A new password must be at least 8 characters and must differ from the current one. After you save, other devices are logged out. This browser stays logged in.

phone.title: 11. Writing on a phone
phone.lead: Open it in the phone’s browser. There is nothing to install.
phone.top: At the top, the left side is Back or the bookshelf, the middle is the book title, and More on the right holds the bookshelf, the guide, profile, and log out.
phone.tabs: After you open a book, the bottom bar is Write, Outline, Memory, Foreshadows, and More. More holds Search, Read, Stats, Versions, and Settings.
phone.write: While you write, the prose fills the screen. “Chapters” at the bottom opens the chapter list. “Generate” or “Continue” is on the right. “Tools” holds the chapter outline, injected context, the consistency check, and edit prose.
phone.outline: In Outline, go from World and Overall outline into a volume, then into a chapter’s outline.
phone.lists: Memory and Foreshadows are full-page lists. Tap a row to edit. To add a character or a setting, tap “New” at the bottom right.

trouble.title: If you run into these
trouble.modelTitle: It says no model is configured
trouble.model: In Settings, fill in the base URL and the key, pick a model for all five tasks, then click “Save model settings”. Generation checks this before it starts writing.
trouble.localTitle: You chose this browser only, and another browser cannot generate
trouble.local: The key is still in the original browser. Enter it again in Settings on the new browser, or switch to “Save on the server (encrypted)”.
trouble.gray: Read the line under the button. Usual reasons: there is no prose yet; the consistency check has not been run; the prose changed after the check and needs to be checked again; a must-fix issue is still open.
trouble.thinkingTitle: Generation stays on “The model is thinking”
trouble.thinking: Reasoning is not written into the prose. Wait until the prose starts, or click “Stop generating”. Text already written stays, and you can continue generating.
trouble.staleTitle: You changed the chapter outline, but the prose is still the old draft
trouble.stale: Existing prose is not rewritten automatically. On the writing page, click “Regenerate”.
trouble.summary: The confirmation itself is already done. On the done page, or in summaries in Memory, click “Regenerate summary”.
trouble.editTitle: You want to edit a chapter that is already confirmed
trouble.edit: If no later chapter is confirmed, undo this chapter’s confirmation on the done page or in version history, then edit.

auth.leadLogin: Log in to return to your bookshelf
auth.hint: Usernames are 2 to 32 characters. Chinese, letters, digits, underscores, and hyphens are allowed. Passwords need at least 8 characters. The first account to register is the admin.
auth.goLogin: Already have an account? Log in
auth.closed: Registration is closed. If the database is empty, you can still register the first admin.
auth.network: Network error. Try again in a moment.
